name: piano_mf
source: Iowa MIS piano mf (pre-2012 collection), 86 keys B0-C8, stereo 44.1k
notes: encoder + template do not exist yet — groundwork config only (see out/piano_analysis_report.md).

Samples are 44.1 kHz vs the engine's 48 kHz render rate. No resampling needed: every refmetrics extractor works in Hz (harmonic_env bins at k*f0, BANDS in Hz, attack rise in seconds), and all analysis bands top out at 8 kHz, far below either Nyquist. Reference is built at 44.1k, candidates analysed at their render rate.

onset_relative: sample lead-in silence varies 0.04-0.54 s across keys, so the clarinet-style file-start-relative windows are wrong for piano. iowa_reference.py must onset-align (first crossing of 2 percent of peak on a 5 ms RMS envelope) before slicing sus/attack windows. NOT yet implemented there.

'sus' windows are really early-decay windows (piano has no sustain); sus_start 0.25 skips the attack, sus_len 1.0 stays inside the prompt-sound segment on all score notes (earliest measured prompt/aftersound break is ~0.9 s at C4/G4 — window ends near the break, acceptable for a level-normalised envelope metric).

A0 and Bb0 do not exist at mf on the Iowa server (confirmed 404, see samples MANIFEST.md). Decision: leave the gap rather than pitch-shift B0 down — a shifted B0 would fabricate reference data with the wrong inharmonicity (B rises toward A0) and wrong hammer spectrum. Lowest reference note is C1; B0 itself is analysed in the report but kept out of score_notes (its fundamental sits below the 30 Hz analysis floor of the attack bands).

motion_samples: piano 'motion' is unison-string beating, not vibrato; derive_motion medians over a 1.0 s early-decay window are usable but expect amp_frac_rms to dominate (beating), resid cents to be small.
